source: SHEET CIRCLE LINE_FCopy JM.pdf (Exercise J-M, 37 questions, marks assumed 4 each)

questions.key_step: Midpoint of a chord subtending θ is at distance R cos(θ/2) from the centre.
questions.justification: Needs the standard chord-midpoint locus radius, then a short trigonometric solve; two routine stages with no real trap. Similar routine-chain demand to 2021-P2-Q7 (L2).

questions.key_step: Decode a+b=0 from the intersection data, then reflect the centre.
questions.justification: Three routine stages (decode points, diameter circle, reflection) with option check available; no insight needed. Chain of routine steps like 2021-P1-Q9 (L2).

questions.key_step: AB is the chord of contact of C, so compare it with the polar.
questions.justification: Standard pole-polar plus a distance; chain of two routine steps with option check, comparable to 2026-P2-Q2 style perpendicular-tangent routine (L3) but easier and numerical coefficients.

questions.key_step: Isosceles triangle makes the incentre lie on the axis x+y=5; excentres also qualify.
questions.justification: Needs vertices, symmetry insight and awareness that an excircle is also tangent to the three lines (option D is the trap); more than a routine chain.

questions.key_step: Roll the centre 4 units along the tangent, reflect in T, then trapezium area.
questions.justification: Four connected stages (tangent direction, translation, reflection, area) with surds; one slip changes the answer, but each step is standard.

questions.key_step: Midpoint (λ,−λ) forces the other end Q=2M−P; D>0 gives the condition.
questions.justification: Non-routine parametrisation of chords bisected by a line followed by a discriminant condition; idea less commonly practised (midpoints of chords from a point).

questions.key_step: Right angle in a semicircle gives α; then tangents at Q and R.
questions.justification: Several routine steps (α, two tangents, intersection, k) with arithmetic; no insight.

questions.key_step: The given line is the chord of contact, compare with the polar of S.
questions.justification: One standard idea (pole-polar) with a short solve; a slightly longer chain than level 1 because the coefficients must be compared.

questions.key_step: OC ⟂ CP and CQ make right triangles, OP²=OC²+CP².
questions.justification: Short but needs a neat observation (area gives CP, then Pythagoras twice); routine geometry.

questions.key_step: Area of the tangent triangle = RL³/(R²+L²) or via the polar.
questions.justification: Tangent length, then standard area formula; routine chain.

questions.key_step: P and Q lie on the circle with diameter OC.
questions.justification: One familiar fact (circle through points of contact has OC as diameter) plus a quadratic; routine.

questions.key_step: Equal chord and radius means a 60° angle; locus of the dividing point is a circle.
questions.justification: Three stages: angle, coordinates, elimination; routine for a prepared student.

questions.key_step: P is a homothetic image of the circle traced by B.
questions.justification: One familiar locus idea followed by one distance; easy.

questions.key_step: Normal through the centre plus equal distance from two tangents; the r<8 constraint rejects one root.
questions.justification: Two-case casework with an absolute-value equation and a rejection step; a slip gives the wrong option.

questions.key_step: d = r1 + r2 so three common tangents.
questions.justification: One familiar comparison of d with the radii; arithmetic only.

questions.key_step: Intersect y=x+1 with the line and the circle; b²+b−4=0.
questions.justification: Region reading plus two intersections; answer is a clean algebraic simplification.

questions.key_step: (α+β−a)²=2αβ from the circle equation.
questions.justification: Numerical format with a non-obvious elimination step (the circle condition collapses the expansion); no options to check.

questions.key_step: Reflect the centre; equal radii give α.
questions.justification: Routine reflection and equating radii; no insight but a multi-step numerical chain.

questions.key_step: Chord of length 2: r² = d² + 1 with d from the centre (r,r).
questions.justification: Standard chord-length relation leads to a quadratic in r; routine numerical.

questions.key_step: Fit the circle through three points and substitute.
questions.justification: Single standard routine step; easy.
One familiar condition, applied once.

questions.key_step: Chord midpoint is the first centre, so R² = r² + d².
questions.justification: Needs the perpendicular-from-centre fact; a few routine steps.

questions.key_step: Minimise OA+OB for a line through (8,2).
questions.justification: Straightforward calculus/AM-GM after finding the centre; routine.

questions.key_step: Condition for two intersections plus the reality constraint 4λ²≥9; then substitute a, b.
questions.justification: Squared-radical inequalities, two conditions and a final substitution into four curves; more precision risk than a routine chain.

questions.key_step: Midpoints of chords through the origin lie on the circle with diameter OC.
questions.justification: Derivation of the locus then a chord length; routine chain.

questions.key_step: Tangent line is at distance r from the centre.
questions.justification: One familiar condition; extra given data is redundant.

questions.key_step: A single-point meeting means a tangent; P is the foot of the perpendicular.
questions.justification: Multi-step chain (centre, line, radius, tangent comparison) with careful fractions, no insight.

questions.key_step: Cosine rule gives α; the common chord is perpendicular to the line of centres.
questions.justification: Numerical, several stages with the principal-value reading of sin⁻¹; no options to check.

questions.key_step: Sides parallel to y=x+3 at distance r/√2 from the centre.
questions.justification: Routine: find sides, intersect, sum; long arithmetic but no insight.

questions.key_step: MN is parallel to PQ at distance 3 from the origin.
questions.justification: Standard chord-distance relation, two sides of the centre need a thought.

questions.key_step: Closest distance = d − r.
questions.justification: One familiar idea after locating the centre.

questions.key_step: Centre on the diagonal at r√2 from C; CF = r√2 + r.
questions.justification: Short geometric chain with a diagram; routine.

questions.key_step: Radical axis S1−S2=0.
questions.justification: One familiar move then a distance.

questions.key_step: Inradius of an equilateral triangle; square in a circle: side² = 2r².
questions.justification: Two direct formulas.

questions.key_step: The point of contact divides the centres in the ratio of the given section.
questions.justification: Section formula and distances; routine multi-step.

questions.key_step: Reflect the point and take the distance from the centre.
questions.justification: One formula, applied once.

questions.key_step: The circle passes through the origin so r = distance of centre from origin; internal tangency.
questions.justification: Needs the observation that r=√(h²+k²) and internal touching; numerical, moderately uncommon idea.
